newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Thursday mainly due to the issue of domestic A shares by Nanjing Zhongda Co on the Shanghai stock exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.60 percent from 9.00 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 4.8 million losts from 2.1 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the increased demand for money supported repo rates, especially those for early-maturing contracts.
"The new issue boosted market activity after the repo rates falls in the past few days," one trader said.
Traders cited renewed market rumours that the central bank might cut bank interest rates and bank reserve ratios, which would prevent any sharp rises in the repo rates.
Traders said they believed the rates were likely to rise further in the next few days due to a large number of new A shares listing just around the corner.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday led by the 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, traders said.
The 10-year bond was the most actively traded, rising to 122.67 yuan from 122.25 yuan.
The first year interest of the bond will be paid on June 14, triggering heavy buying, traders said.
Interest on the bond is paid annually, unlike the most exisiting contracts which pay on maturity.
Traders said buying in the 10-year bond boosted market sentiment, which in turn led investors to build positions in other contracts as well, pushing up prices.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to a heavy 2.2 million lots from 1.5 million lots.
Traders said the 10-year bond has the potential to rise further in the coming few days, possibly pushing the whole spot market up.
